author: mvafin
title: Windows CC build fails with compiler/linker out-of-memory errors under high parallelism
signature: Windows Release build runs out of memory - compiler fatal error C1060 (out of heap space) and linker fatal error LNK1102 (out of memory) under high parallelism|Infrastructure

failed_jobs.name: Conditional Compilation
failed_jobs.symptom: cl.exe fatal error C1060 (compiler out of heap space) during parallel MSBuild compilation of onednn/intel_cpu and core/reference sources

failed_jobs.name: ci/gha_overall_status_windows_cc
failed_jobs.symptom: Overall status check failed because the Conditional Compilation build job failed

key_errors: cl : command line  warning D9014: invalid value '15' for '/cgthreads'; assuming '4' [openvino_runtime_obj.vcxproj]
c1xx : fatal  error C1060: compiler is out of heap space [src\inference\openvino_runtime_obj.vcxproj]
cl : command line  error D8000: UNKNOWN COMMAND-LINE ERROR [src\plugins\intel_cpu\thirdparty\onednn\src\cpu\dnnl_cpu.vcxproj]
xbyak.h(1929,2): error C1060: compiler is out of heap space [dnnl_cpu.vcxproj]
algorithm(5545,117): error C1060: compiler is out of heap space
root_cause: The Windows Conditional Compilation build invokes MSBuild with a parallelism level that requests 15 code-generation threads per cl.exe process ('/cgthreads:15', downgraded with warning D9014 to 4), while also running many parallel cl.exe instances across vcxproj files (openvino_runtime_obj, onednn dnnl_cpu, core reference, etc). On the GitHub-hosted Windows runner's limited RAM, this combined parallelism exhausts available heap for the MSVC front-end (c1xx), causing fatal error C1060 'compiler is out of heap space' and a cascading UNKNOWN COMMAND-LINE ERROR D8000 across multiple concurrently-building projects. This is a resource-exhaustion failure of the CI runner/build configuration, unrelated to the specific commit's diff. The merged PR #40251 only touches src/frontends/gguf and genai mask logic (2 files, +14/-4) and has no plausible connection to a Windows MSVC heap exhaustion during an unrelated CPU plugin/onednn compilation.
reproduction_steps: N/A - resource-exhaustion failure tied to Windows runner RAM/parallelism; not reliably reproducible locally. To attempt reproduction: build the CC preset locally on a memory-constrained Windows VM with the same /MP or cmake parallel job count as CI and the same /cgthreads setting, and simultaneously build the onednn and openvino_runtime_obj targets.
recommended_actions: Reduce the cl.exe parallel job count (CMAKE_BUILD_PARALLEL_LEVEL / MSBuild /m / /cgthreads) specifically for the Windows Conditional Compilation workflow to lower peak memory use.
Investigate switching the Windows CC runner to a larger-memory runner SKU, since this is the 25th recorded occurrence of the same signature in under a month.
Consider splitting the onednn/intel_cpu heavy compilation units into smaller translation units or disabling unnecessary heavy headers (e.g. xbyak) in the CC build configuration.
Add retry-with-reduced-parallelism logic to the Windows CC job so a single heap-exhaustion failure doesn't block post-commit CI.
prevention_strategies: Cap parallel compilation jobs/threads on Windows CI runners to a level validated against available RAM; monitor peak memory usage of Windows builds and alert before it causes OOM. Treat repeated C1060/D8000 errors on the Windows CC workflow as an infrastructure capacity issue to be fixed at the CI configuration level rather than re-investigated per commit.
historical_context: This exact signature (Windows Release build runs out of memory - C1060/LNK1102 under high parallelism) has now been recorded 25 times since 2026-11-03, with runs recurring nearly daily (most recently 2026-11-24T14:47:10Z and 11:33:31Z, prior to this one). No past resolution has been recorded in the pattern database; this remains an open, unresolved recurring infrastructure issue.
